rows.grounds: compound naming Śeṣa and other nāga rulers

items.question: How do the serpent kings praise the lord who transcends all remainder?
premises: Śeṣa and other serpent kings sing praise.
The addressed lord is called lord of remainder.
The lord is also beyond even that remainder.
items.inference: Serpent kings honor the deity as sovereign over and transcendent to all residual existence.
uncertainties: Exact nuance of kṛtaśeṣaśeṣam is interpretive.
items.plain_english: The serpent kings, led by Śeṣa, sing to you as the lord of the remainder and as the one who leaves even that remainder behind.

rows.grounds: group to which the flocks belong

items.question: How do the most skilled flocks of birds honor the lord of birds?
premises: Bird groups are most skilled in twofold motion.
They address the deity as lord of birds.
They fan him around in service.
items.inference: The birds express devotion by using their supreme skill in flight to serve the bird-lord.
uncertainties: dvidhā gatau may refer to specific modes of flight.
items.plain_english: The most skilled flocks of birds, moving in two ways, fan you around as the lord of birds.

rows.grounds: state of the herd while bowing

items.question: Why does the herd of deer bow to the five-faced lord?
premises: The deer herd bows to the deity.
The bowing is for obtaining grace.
The herd has cast off pride.
items.inference: Humble devotion from the animal realm seeks the grace of the five-faced lord.
items.plain_english: The herd of deer, having cast off pride, bows to you, the five-faced lord, seeking your grace.

rows.grounds: present participle describing the elephant group

items.question: How does the elephant group offer praise through music and satisfaction?
premises: The elephant group uses instruments including burbura sounds.
It satisfies through these musical means.
It also sings in praise.
items.inference: The elephants honor the deity through both instrumental offering and song.
uncertainties: nijāṅganāburburakādivādyaiḥ may include bodily or female-associated sounds.
items.plain_english: And the elephant group sings, satisfying you with instruments such as the burbura and others of their own kind.

items.question: Why do horses call the incomparable lord with their neighing sounds?
premises: Horses call with distinctive neighing sounds.
They invite the deity to mount them.
They regard him as their incomparable own lord.
items.inference: The horses express devoted service by offering themselves as mounts to their supreme lord.
items.plain_english: With their neighing sounds, they call you, the incomparable lord, to mount them as their own master.

rows.grounds: group characterized by movement and sound

items.question: Why does the group of moving creatures search everywhere for the unobstructed lord?
premises: The group of moving and vocal creatures searches here and there.
It seeks the one whose movement is unobstructed.
The search is for the sake of satisfaction.
items.inference: All moving beings seek the freely moving lord in order to attain fulfillment.
uncertainties: vāścāravargo is an unusual compound; sense inferred from members.
items.plain_english: The group of creatures that move and call also searches here and there for you, whose movement is unobstructed, in order to find satisfaction.

rows.grounds: epithet suggesting adornment or dominion over kali time

items.question: Why does the assembly of great herbs bow to the moon-crested lord?
premises: The group of great herbs bows in reverence.
The lord bears the moon as his crest.
The lord is described with a garland of the kali age.
items.inference: Even the realm of great herbs honors the lord who bears cosmic and temporal insignia.
items.plain_english: O lord, the assembly of great herbs bows to you, who wear the moon as your crest and bear the garland of the age of Kali.

rows.grounds: abiding in both transcendent and immanent levels

items.question: What paradoxical nature defines the supreme lord's play across higher and lower realms?
premises: The lord is supreme and indescribable.
He abides in both higher and lower states.
His play is at once playless and singular play.
items.inference: The deity's sport transcends ordinary opposition by uniting play and playlessness across all levels.
uncertainties: akhelaikakakhelakhelaḥ is a dense compound with interpretive flexibility.
items.plain_english: This supreme, indescribable one, abiding in both the higher and the lower, plays as the playless one whose play is a single, unique sport.

rows.grounds: state of being divided into varieties
agent who creates difference and division

items.question: How does the maker of difference produce differentiation through concealment and unveiling?
premises: Differentiation arises from gradations of covering and unveiling.
This differentiation is produced by a maker of difference and division.
The process belongs to the lord's own activity.
items.inference: Multiplicity is generated by the deity's graded self-concealment and self-revelation.
items.plain_english: Differentiation arises from the gradation of his own covering and unveiling, wrought by the maker of difference and division.

rows.grounds: object not to be clung to

items.question: Why do adherents of limited vision mistake their own doctrine for the true essence?
premises: Those fixed in small vision do not grasp insistence properly.
They know only their own speech.
They take that speech as the very essence.
items.inference: Limited perspectives absolutize their own partial doctrine as ultimate truth.
uncertainties: na grāhitā āgraham can be read in more than one syntactic way.
items.plain_english: Adherents of limited vision do not take insistence rightly; they know only their own doctrine and regard it as the very essence.

rows.grounds: necessary grace or descent of power
leading to or grounded in nothingness
one's own inner wealth or awareness

items.question: Why is the descent of supreme power necessary for knowing one's own awareness?
premises: Without the descent of supreme power they know nothing.
The knowledge sought is of one's own awareness.
That awareness is described as going to nothingness.
items.inference: Recognition of one's true awareness depends on the grace of supreme power, not ordinary effort alone.
uncertainties: akiñcanagāṃ may mean tending toward egolessness or poverty of self.
items.plain_english: Without the descent of supreme power, they know nothing of their own awareness, which leads to the state of having nothing.

rows.grounds: means arising from the deity's own expansion
in the knower of each particular form

items.question: How are the means for manifesting the lord ultimately the lord's own expansions?
premises: The means exist for the manifestation of the lord.
They operate through the lord's own expansion.
They belong to the lord alone in each knower.
items.inference: All spiritual means are expressions of the deity's own power within the knowing subject.
uncertainties: tvatprathiā is read as instrumental sense from context.
items.plain_english: The means for your manifestation are your own expansions and belong to you alone, present in each knower who knows.

items.question: How does devotion to the lord establish abiding in a peaceful inner state?
premises: There is withdrawal from the external.
There is also withdrawal inwardly.
This abiding in a peaceful state occurs through devotion to the lord.
items.inference: Devotion enables both outer and inner withdrawal, culminating in peaceful abiding.
items.plain_english: Here, through devotion to you, there is withdrawal from the outer and also within, and this becomes abiding in a peaceful state.

items.question: How can a weak yet shining awareness remove obstacles by uniting twofold experience?
premises: Even what is weak can gain strength.
It shines as one state within twofold experience.
In that condition it removes obstacles.
items.inference: Awareness, though initially weak, becomes effective when it shines as a unified ground of dual experience.
uncertainties: The exact object removed by haranty is unstated.
items.plain_english: Even when weak, once it has gained strength and shines as a single state within twofold experience, it removes them.

items.question: What happens to the powers when awareness becomes contracted and seeks support?
premises: In contraction, awareness rests on support.
At that time its powers appear.
Those powers do not shine in the same way.
items.inference: Contraction alters the manifestation of powers so they no longer appear in their prior fullness.
uncertainties: The referent of support in ālambate is implicit.
items.plain_english: When contracted, it then takes support; its powers shine, but not in the same way as before.

rows.grounds: ego based on incompleteness and related notions
lacking the wealth of supreme power

items.question: Why is the one who identifies with incompleteness impoverished despite supreme power's wealth?
premises: A person may assume the ego of incompleteness.
Such a thinker is poor.
This poverty is in relation to the wealth of supreme power.
items.inference: Identification with incompleteness veils the inherent wealth of supreme power.
items.plain_english: The one who takes himself to be incomplete and the like is poor in the wealth of supreme power.

rows.grounds: sole cause at the outset of creation
shining within what is to be manifested

items.question: How does the sole cause of creation repeatedly shine within manifestation?
premises: There is a sole cause at the beginning of creation.
Manifestation and related processes arise repeatedly.
That cause shines within what is manifested.
items.inference: The same ultimate cause continually manifests and illumines the field of appearance.
uncertainties: The grammatical subject is carried over from context.
items.plain_english: Again and again, as the sole cause at the beginning of creation, it shines in manifestation and within what is to be manifested.

rows.grounds: refers to the previously mentioned power or state
state of being the great lord

items.question: How does the unveiling of that power reveal one's own great lordship?
premises: Through that unveiling, something becomes clear.
What becomes clear is great lordship.
This lordship is one's own inherent nature.
items.inference: The revelation of that power discloses the subject's innate sovereignty as great lord.
uncertainties: The antecedent of tasyās is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: Through her unveiling, this one's own great lordship indeed becomes clearly manifest.

items.question: How does touching the nature of consciousness restore one's supreme omnipotence?
premises: One apprehends the own-nature of consciousness.
After that apprehension one attains omnipotence again.
That omnipotence is one's own and supreme.
items.inference: Direct recognition of consciousness's nature restores the subject's inherent supreme power.
items.plain_english: Having touched the own-nature of consciousness, one again attains that supreme omnipotence which is one's own.

rows.grounds: known only by one's own experience

items.question: How does time, known only by one's own experience, burn away particular natures instantly?
premises: Time is measurable only by one's own experience.
It acts in each particular nature.
It burns that nature in a mere instant.
items.inference: Experiential time instantly consumes differentiated forms within their own natures.
uncertainties: Subject-object relation between kālaḥ and adaḥ is interpretive.
items.plain_english: Time, known only through one's own experience, burns that away in each particular nature in a single instant.

items.question: How does the self-dependent reality directly produce the range from Sadāśiva to inert matter?
premises: The range extends from Sadāśiva to the inert level.
This whole range is made directly.
The making is self-dependent.
items.inference: The autonomous self directly generates the entire spectrum of reality from highest to lowest.
items.plain_english: It directly makes this whole range, from Sadāśiva down to the inert level, as something self-dependent.

rows.grounds: state centered on the body and such

items.question: How can one remain completely liberated while still experiencing the body-centered state?
premises: The body-centered state may still be perceived.
Even so, one can roam freely.
That roaming is completely liberated.
items.inference: Liberation can coexist with embodied experience when awareness remains free in its activity.
items.plain_english: Even while the body-centered state is being perceived, one roams about completely liberated.

rows.grounds: in the shining expansion of the middle

items.question: How do the renowned means culminate in the shining expansion of the middle state?
premises: The renowned means are ultimately resorted to.
They are firm through reasoning.
Their culmination is in the shining expansion of the middle.
items.inference: Established spiritual methods ultimately converge in the luminous central expansion.
uncertainties: madhyavikāsabhāse may refer to a specific technical state.
items.plain_english: In the end, those renowned means, firmly grounded in reasoning, come to rest in the shining expansion of the middle.

rows.grounds: knower of the power of one's own parts marked by eleven

items.question: How does the knower of the elevenfold powers cherish absorption moment by moment?
premises: There is a knower of the power of one's own parts marked by eleven.
This knower acts moment by moment.
The action is cherishing absorption.
items.inference: Mastery of the elevenfold powers sustains contemplative absorption continuously in every moment.
uncertainties: The precise referent of ekādaśāṅka is tradition-specific.
items.plain_english: The knower of the power of his own parts marked by eleven cherishes absorption moment by moment.
